Another study observed a worsening trend in anxiety and depression between 6 and 12 months after COVID-19 onset.

A meta-analysis of 2655 SARS-CoV-2 patients across 28 studies identified ground glass opacity as the typical HRCT feature of COVID-19, present in 71.64% of patients, often with associated consolidation and other abnormalities.

In a retrospective study of 66 primary Sjögren's syndrome patients with interstitial lung involvement, ground glass opacity was seen on HRCT in 87.88% of patients, with septal/subpleural lines in 81.82%, subpleural cysts in 40.90%, honeycombing in 28.79%, and pleural margin irregularities in 21%.
Nonspecific interstitial pneumonia (NSIP) is reported as the most frequent radiological pattern of interstitial lung disease in primary Sjögren's syndrome patients.

Pozzi et al. described three patients with connective tissue disease-related interstitial lung disease initially misattributed to SARS-CoV-2 pneumonia, whose respiratory failure and arthritis greatly improved after immunosuppressive therapy.
Serum tryptase measurement is important for diagnosing anaphylaxis and for identifying underlying mast cell disorders.
In infants and toddlers, anaphylaxis symptoms may present differently than in older children and adults, and patient age does not correlate with reaction severity.
If epinephrine is administered promptly and the patient has a prompt, complete, and durable response, immediate activation of emergency medical services may not be required.

For most medical indications, the risk of stopping or changing beta-blocker or ACE inhibitor medication may exceed the risk of more severe anaphylaxis if the medication is continued, particularly in patients with insect sting anaphylaxis.
Evaluation for mastocytosis, including bone marrow biopsy, should be considered for adult patients with severe insect sting anaphylaxis or recurrent idiopathic anaphylaxis.
After perioperative anaphylaxis, repeat anesthesia may proceed via shared decision-making guided by history and diagnostic evaluation including skin tests, in vitro tests, or supervised challenge.
Infusion of levcromakalim, a KATP channel opener, induced cluster headache attacks in 60% of participants with episodic cluster headache during a bout, compared with 10% after placebo.
In participants in the attack-free remission period, levcromakalim did not significantly increase cluster headache attack incidence compared with placebo.
Among participants with chronic cluster headache, 29% experienced attacks after levcromakalim infusion compared with none after placebo.
The authors propose that KATP channel inhibitors could serve as a therapeutic strategy for cluster headache based on the provocation results.

The 2020 European Headache Federation criteria define resistant migraine as failure of at least three preventive drug classes and refractory migraine as failure of all available preventive classes, both requiring at least 8 monthly debilitating headache days.
An international survey (BARR) found that resistant and refractory migraine patients are seen far more frequently by headache specialists than by general neurologists or primary care physicians.
Oral migraine preventive drugs provide only a modest therapeutic gain over placebo in reducing headache days.
CGRP-targeting monoclonal antibodies reduce monthly migraine days more than placebo, and more than oral preventatives.
Even among patients with a good (50-74%) reduction in migraine days after erenumab, a substantial fraction still had a high residual monthly migraine burden.
Topiramate causes more adverse events in individuals treated for migraine than in those treated for epilepsy, suggesting disease-specific tolerability differences.
Adherence to oral migraine preventive treatment drops sharply over the first year.
Whole-genome sequencing found no genetic variants associated with chronic migraine, suggesting migraine chronification is driven mainly by environmental rather than genetic factors.

An MRI study found diffusion abnormalities in multiple deep brain structures (thalamus, caudate, putamen, pallidum, amygdala, brainstem, white matter) in individuals with refractory migraine compared with headache-free controls.
CGRP levels are higher in individuals with chronic migraine than in those with episodic migraine or healthy controls.
The efficacy of olanzapine in individuals for whom CGRP monoclonal antibodies have failed suggests dopaminergic dysfunction may drive migraine refractoriness.
The endocannabinoid anti-nociceptive and anti-inflammatory system may be less functional in individuals with chronic migraine than those with episodic migraine.
In a subgroup analysis of the FOCUS trial, patients with more prior treatment failures showed reduced placebo response but no reduction in fremanezumab's actual drug efficacy.
Real-world evidence suggests that a high number of prior preventive treatment failures may predict non-response to CGRP monoclonal antibodies, in contrast to RCT subgroup findings.
Real-world studies of CGRP monoclonal antibodies in individuals with multiple preventive treatment failures showed 30-51% achieving a ≥50% reduction in monthly migraine days at 3 months.

Rimegepant and atogepant, oral CGRP-pathway antagonists, were superior to placebo in reducing monthly migraine days and achieving ≥50% response rates in individuals with episodic or chronic migraine and up to four preventive treatment failures.
The HER-MES double-blind RCT demonstrated that erenumab has higher tolerability and adherence than topiramate.
Unlike oral preventatives, available data do not indicate a loss of treatment effect over time with drugs antagonising the CGRP pathway.
RCTs showed occipital nerve stimulation is superior to sham in reducing headache days, pain intensity, and disability in refractory chronic migraine, though with adverse events.
The EVENT RCT found no efficacy of transcutaneous vagal nerve stimulation in individuals with chronic migraine.

A UK real-world audit of daily sTMS in patients with at least three preventive treatment failures showed a median reduction of 5 monthly headache days at 3 months, with 60% achieving ≥30% reduction, and 45% maintaining sustained response at 12 months.

Real-world studies of high-frequency spinal cord stimulation showed long-term decreases in monthly migraine days and improved quality of life, with about half of patients converting from chronic to episodic migraine.
Real-world data suggest that individuals with a shorter duration of chronic migraine respond better to onabotulinumtoxinA than those with longer disease duration.
A German study found erenumab was more effective when reimbursement was allowed after only one prior preventive failure, compared with stricter reimbursement conditions requiring more failures.
Real-world evidence suggests that individuals with a high number of prior preventive treatment failures may be less likely to respond to CGRP monoclonal antibodies.

Rimegepant and atogepant, oral CGRP-pathway antagonists, were superior to placebo in reducing monthly migraine days and achieving ≥50% response in individuals with episodic or chronic migraine, including those with up to four prior preventive failures.
Both CGRP monoclonal antibodies and onabotulinumtoxinA show a very low proportion of treatment discontinuation due to lack of efficacy or adverse events.
The HER-MES double-blind RCT found erenumab had higher tolerability and adherence compared with topiramate.
Gepants did not cause more adverse events than placebo in randomized controlled trials.
Unlike oral migraine preventatives, available data do not indicate a loss of treatment effect over time with drugs antagonising the CGRP pathway.

Case series and retrospective studies showed possible efficacy of dual therapy combining onabotulinumtoxinA and CGRP monoclonal antibodies in individuals who had not responded to most available treatments.
RCTs found a synergistic, rather than merely additive, benefit when combining pharmacologic treatment with behavioural therapy for migraine.

RCTs demonstrated occipital nerve stimulation was superior to sham for achieving 50% reduction in headache days, reducing pain intensity, and reducing disability in individuals with refractory chronic migraine, though at the cost of adverse events.
The EVENT RCT did not demonstrate efficacy of transcutaneous vagal nerve stimulation in individuals with chronic migraine.

A UK real-world clinical audit of daily single-pulse transcranial magnetic stimulation in individuals with at least three prior preventive treatment failures found a median reduction of 5.0 monthly headache days at 3 months, with 60% achieving at least a 30% reduction, and 45% maintaining a sustained response at 12 months.

Real-world studies of high-frequency spinal cord stimulation showed a long-term (>1 year) decrease in monthly migraine days and improved quality of life, with about half of participants converting from chronic to episodic migraine.
Real-world data suggest that individuals with a shorter duration of chronic migraine respond better to onabotulinumtoxinA than those with a longer disease duration.
A German study found erenumab was more effective when reimbursement was allowed after only one prior preventive treatment failure compared with under stricter reimbursement criteria.
A five-day course of IVIG produced dramatic improvement in mental status, with the patient's MoCA score improving from 17/30 to 26/30 by discharge.
FDG-PET brain imaging showed hypermetabolism in bilateral basal ganglia, superior/middle frontal gyri, and olfactory cortex, consistent with the early pattern of autoimmune encephalitis.

A follow-up FDG-PET scan one week after IVIG showed a global decrease in cortical brain metabolism, most pronounced in the basal ganglia, frontal gyri, and olfactory cortex, reflecting treatment response.
The patient's serum SARS-CoV-2 IgG was markedly elevated (1781 mg/dl) prior to IVIG therapy, and this elevation correlated with worsening mental status and fatigue.
Periodic IVIG infusions every two weeks produced a sustained reduction in the patient's IgG level, correlated with remarkable improvement in mental status and anxiety symptoms.
A spike in IgG level was observed in February 2022 associated with COVID-19 vaccination, though improvement in mental status/behavioral facets continued afterward.
Despite periodic IVIG infusions, the patient continued to show severe impairment in verbal memory and cognitive interference (Stroop task) on repeated neuropsychological evaluations in 2022 and 2023.

During periodic IVIG infusions, the patient's anxiety, irritability, and insomnia improved significantly without any change in his psychotropic medication doses (sertraline 200 mg, quetiapine 100 mg).
The patient's serum anti-nuclear antibody was positive (1:160, speckled pattern), while anti-NMDA receptor antibody titer was negative, supporting a diagnosis of seronegative autoimmune encephalitis.
Lumbar puncture revealed newly elevated CSF protein (54 mg/dl versus normal range 15-45 mg/dl) with negative pleocytosis, negative CSF SARS-CoV-2, and negative CSF Lyme antigen.

The authors postulate that the patient's lack of steroid treatment during his initial COVID-19 pneumonia admission may have contributed to the subsequent development of autoimmune encephalitis and cognitive deficits.

Working memory and processing speed deficits identified on neuropsychological testing correlated with the patient's real-world difficulties managing financial affairs and complex tasks, while basic ADLs remained intact.
Autoimmune thyroiditis was present concomitantly in 19.6% of patients with primary Sjögren's syndrome.
Patients with pSS and concomitant autoimmune thyroiditis had a lower prevalence of lymphoma compared with pSS patients without autoimmune thyroiditis.
Male sex was less prevalent among pSS patients with concomitant autoimmune thyroiditis than among those without.
DMARD use was lower and remained significantly lower on multivariable analysis in pSS patients with concomitant autoimmune thyroiditis compared with those without.
Fibromyalgia was more prevalent in pSS patients with concomitant autoimmune thyroiditis than in those without, and this remained significant after multivariable adjustment.
Coeliac disease was more prevalent in pSS patients with concomitant autoimmune thyroiditis, confirmed on multivariable analysis.
Hypergammaglobulinaemia was more prevalent among pSS patients with concomitant autoimmune thyroiditis than among those without.
In a histology subgroup, minor salivary gland focus score was significantly lower in pSS patients with autoimmune thyroiditis compared with those without.
Multivariable analysis confirmed that coeliac disease was more prevalent in pSS patients with concomitant autoimmune thyroiditis compared to those without.
Multivariable analysis confirmed that use of disease-modifying anti-rheumatic drugs (DMARDs) was lower in pSS patients with concomitant autoimmune thyroiditis compared to those without.
In a histology subgroup, patients with pSS but without autoimmune thyroiditis had a significantly higher minor salivary gland focus score than those with concomitant autoimmune thyroiditis.
In the same histology subgroup, the number of lymphocytic foci in minor salivary glands was significantly higher in pSS patients without autoimmune thyroiditis than in those with it.
Among 15 patients with isolated Lambl's excrescences, 8 presented with migraine-like headache, supporting an association between this cardiac valvular structure and migraine-like headache.
Among the 8 patients with Lambl's excrescences-associated migraine-like headache, 3 experienced visual aura.

Six of the 8 patients with Lambl's excrescences-associated migraine-like headache showed infarct-like lesions on brain MRI, with 2 developing new lesions after their first visit, supporting a microembolic mechanism.

During follow-up, the 4 patients who underwent intervention for Lambl's excrescences had markedly reduced headache recurrence compared with the 4 patients treated only with migraine preventive medication.
A 50-year-old female with chronic migraine and multiple autoimmune markers received an initial 240 mg dose of galcanezumab after failing other migraine treatments.

Following the injection, the patient developed a delayed systemic allergic reaction with injection site reaction, malar erythema, flu-like symptoms, and swelling of the lips and throat requiring emergency treatment.

The patient's history of autoimmune disease, including Hashimoto's disease, positive antinuclear antibody, and positive anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide antibody, is proposed as a predisposing factor for the systemic allergic reaction to galcanezumab.
The patient with chronic migraine also had a pre-existing mast cell disorder, alongside Hashimoto's disease and positive autoimmune serologies.
Galcanezumab is a humanized monoclonal antibody that binds calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP), a neuropeptide implicated in neurogenic inflammation during migraine attacks.
The patient's remaining systemic allergic symptoms improved after a course of oral corticosteroids following initial intravenous steroid and antihistamine treatment for airway symptoms.
The authors suggest that a history of autoimmune disorder may predispose patients to delayed systemic allergic reactions to galcanezumab.
The patient had a documented mast cell disorder, Hashimoto's disease, positive antinuclear antibody, and positive anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide antibody prior to receiving galcanezumab.
Response rates for functional constipation did not differ significantly between children on combined prucalopride plus conventional therapy versus conventional therapy alone.
Hypermobility spectrum disorder was present as a comorbidity in 37% of pediatric patients treated for functional constipation with prucalopride.
Mood disorders were a common comorbidity, present in 49% of the pediatric functional constipation cohort.
Prucalopride combined therapy was associated with improvement of concurrent functional upper GI symptoms in 56% of treated patients.
Hypermobility spectrum disorder was a common comorbidity, present in 37% of pediatric patients with functional constipation in this cohort.
Mood disorders were present in 49% of the pediatric functional constipation cohort as a comorbidity.
Functional upper GI symptoms co-occurred with functional constipation in 84% of the cohort, and dysphagia co-occurred in 12%.
Among patients with a known mood disorder treated with prucalopride, four (7%) reported worsened mood, and two of these endorsed suicidal ideation.
In 2019 the global age-standardized prevalence of tension-type headache was 25,113 per 100,000, higher than that of migraine.
In 2019 the global age-standardized prevalence of migraine was 14,107 per 100,000, lower than tension-type headache but with much greater disability impact.
Tension-type headache prevalence changed only marginally (+0.3%) between 1990 and 2019.
Migraine prevalence increased by 2.8% between 1990 and 2019, a change attributed in part to headache-awareness campaigns.
Years-lived-with-disability rates attributed to tension-type headache in 2019 were far lower than those attributed to migraine.
Migraine accounted for substantially higher years-lived-with-disability rates than tension-type headache in 2019.
YLD rates for tension-type headache were essentially stable between 1990 and 2019.
YLD rates for migraine were basically stable between 1990 and 2019, indicating the disease burden has not lessened despite treatment advances.
Headache disorders directly affect 35% of the global population.
Headache disorder prevalence rises to 50% among females aged 35-39 years, indicating a marked sex-related disparity.
Indirect costs (mainly productivity losses) account for more than 90% of the total economic costs of headache disorders.
Approximately one-third of headaches presenting in African, Middle-East and Asian countries were secondary headaches, most commonly attributed to substances or their withdrawal.
Headache occurred in nearly half of patients during the acute phase of COVID-19 infection, more often in non-hospitalized than hospitalized patients.
Headache prevalence declined over time following COVID-19, from 10.2% at 30 days to 8.4% after 180 days post-infection.
Headache was the third most common symptom after SARS-CoV-2 vaccination, occurring more frequently than in placebo recipients and increasing after the second dose.
Post-traumatic headache was identified in 27-33% of patients over a six-month period following mild traumatic brain injury.
Persistent post-traumatic headache has an estimated 1-year prevalence of 0.21% and a lifetime prevalence of 2.4-4.7%, though data are considered uncertain due to underrecognized mild TBI.
Around 60% of children and adolescents experience headache and around 8% experience migraine over periods ranging from 3 months to lifetime.
Migraine prevalence rises with age, from 5.8% in children under 14 and 7.7% in those under 20, to 14% in adulthood.
Tobacco exposure is associated with a worse clinical profile, including chronification, in cluster headache.
Pain prevalence (largely attributed to headache or back pain) is projected to increase 10-20% over 10 years, with new pain onset predicted by fatigue, sleep disorders and obesity.
Three-quarters of the global burden of nervous system disorders falls on low- and middle-income countries (LMICs).
Headache disorders, and migraine in particular, act as risk factors for cerebrovascular, cardiovascular, visual, perceptual and psychiatric disorders.

Multiple modifiable behavioral and comorbid risk factors—including medication overuse, ineffective acute treatment, obesity, diabetes, hypertension, stressful life events, night-shift work, depression, sleep problems, temporomandibular disorders, physical inactivity, smoking, and alcohol use—are associated with the development of chronic migraine.
Across 18 RCTs, non-pharmacological interventions (tilt training, physical counter pressure maneuvers, yoga) significantly reduced recurrence of vasovagal syncope compared with control.
Subgroup analysis found yoga had the largest effect in reducing vasovagal syncope recurrence compared to control.
Subgroup analysis found tilt training had the smallest, though still significant, effect in reducing vasovagal syncope recurrence compared to control among the interventions studied.
Physical counter pressure maneuvers significantly reduced vasovagal syncope recurrence compared to control.
Anti-NMDAr autoimmune encephalitis includes autonomic nervous system dysfunction such as tachycardia or bradycardia, hyperthermia, and hemodynamic alterations among its clinical manifestations.
Anti-CASPR2 encephalitis, often presenting as Morvan syndrome, includes autonomic nervous system disorders along with neuro-myotonia, memory disorders, and sleep disturbance.
Anti-NMDAr encephalitis shows a strong female predominance, with a women to men ratio of 8:2, occurring mainly during the second decade of life.
Autoimmune and paraneoplastic encephalitis have an incidence of 0.8-1.2 per 100,000 people, comparable to the ~1 per 100,000 incidence of infectious encephalitis.
Hospitalization costs for autoimmune/paraneoplastic encephalitis are markedly higher for patients requiring ICU care compared with those managed on a general ward.
An 'extreme delta brush' EEG pattern is observed in about one third of anti-NMDAr encephalitis cases.
First-line treatment for anti-NMDAr autoimmune encephalitis typically combines high-dose corticosteroids with intravenous immunoglobulin or plasma exchange.
Second-line treatment for refractory anti-NMDAr encephalitis consists of the anti-CD20 monoclonal antibody Rituximab or Cyclophosphamide if there is no improvement with first-line therapy.

Experimental agents Tocilizumab (anti-IL-6 monoclonal antibody) and Bortezomib (proteasome inhibitor) have been tried in small case series for refractory anti-NMDAr encephalitis but have not proven efficacy in large-scale studies.
Survivors of anti-NMDAr autoimmune encephalitis have an approximately 20% risk of relapse in the first years after the initial episode.
Up to 80% of patients with anti-LGI1 encephalitis achieve remission with immunotherapy, though one third relapse.
Anti-AMPAr encephalitis mainly affects females aged 50-60 and is associated with malignancy (commonly breast, thymus, or lung cancer) in about two-thirds of cases.

Diagnosis of autoimmune encephalitis when antibody testing is negative requires simultaneous fulfillment of four criteria: subacute progressive course under three months, bilateral temporal lobe FLAIR/T2 MRI lesions, CSF pleocytosis or epileptiform/reduced-activity EEG changes in temporal lobes, and exclusion of alternative causes.
Survivors of anti-NMDAr autoimmune encephalitis have approximately a 20% risk of relapse within the first years after the initial episode.
Delay in initiating treatment, prolonged ICU length of stay, sepsis, ventilator-associated pneumonia, and tracheostomy are associated with poor prognosis in autoimmune encephalitis.
Anti-LGI1 encephalitis is most commonly associated with thymoma.
Anti-LGI1 encephalitis is frequently characterized by ultra-resistant status epilepticus and REM sleep disturbances.
LGI1 protein acts as a ligand for ADAM22 and ADAM23, proteins with a key role in epilepsy induction, explaining the frequent association of anti-LGI1 encephalitis with treatment-resistant epilepsy.
Up to 80% of anti-LGI1 encephalitis patients achieve remission with immunotherapy, but one third relapse.
Anti-CASPR2 encephalitis typically has an onset around age 65 and, unlike other autoimmune encephalitides, is rarely associated with malignancy except occasionally thymoma.
Anti-AMPAr encephalitis mainly affects females aged 50-60 and is associated with malignancy (breast, thymus, or lung cancer) in two thirds of cases.
Anti-Hu antibodies are more prevalent in lower brainstem damage, while anti-Ma antibodies are more common in upper brainstem damage in paraneoplastic brainstem encephalitis.
Seminoma-associated paraneoplastic encephalitis is most commonly linked to anti-Hu and anti-Ma2 antibodies in the CSF.

Paraneoplastic encephalomyelitis affecting multiple nervous system regions is most commonly associated with anti-Hu antibodies and small cell lung cancer, with the underlying malignancy often difficult to diagnose early.

Limbic encephalitis is most often associated with small cell lung cancer, thymoma, seminoma, breast cancer, and Hodgkin's lymphoma, but in more than half of cases no clinical or imaging evidence of malignancy is found.

In patients with fibromyalgia, tACS applied over the left primary motor cortex for 10 sessions did not produce significant improvements in pain severity or physical function compared to sham stimulation.

In patients with chronic low back pain, tACS applied over bilateral frontal lobe significantly reduced pain severity (DVPRS) compared to sham stimulation, though disability (ODI) was not significantly improved.
The increase in alpha oscillations was significantly greater after tACS than after sham stimulation in patients with chronic low back pain.
In a second chronic low back pain trial, twice as many patients were classified as responders (≥2-point DVPRS decrease) after tACS versus sham, but this difference was not statistically significant.

In patients with chronic migraine, the proportion of migraine attacks terminated without need for rescue medication was significantly higher after tACS applied over the occipital lobe than after sham stimulation.
Pain severity measured by NRS during migraine attacks was significantly lower after tACS than after sham stimulation at 2 and 4 hours post-stimulation.
Prior studies found that the amplitude of alpha oscillations in the brain was negatively correlated with the severity of chronic pain, consistent with pain perception suppressing alpha oscillations.
Studies using EEG and MEG showed that the peak frequency of neuronal oscillations was lower in patients with chronic pain compared with healthy controls.
Changes in gamma frequency (30–100 Hz) neural oscillations in the prefrontal brain area are related to chronic pain.

Abnormal activation of the thalamocortical circuit, evidenced by increased theta rhythm in the anterior cingulate and frontal cortex, is considered a key pathology underlying chronic pain, described as thalamocortical dysrhythmia.
Cognitive dysfunction was present in 45% of the 127 reviewed anti-IgLON5 disease case reports.
REM-sleep behavioral disorder was reported in 15% of anti-IgLON5 disease cases.
Parkinsonism was reported in 14% of anti-IgLON5 disease cases.
Respiratory insufficiency was reported in 37% of anti-IgLON5 disease cases.
Bulbar symptoms were reported in 67% of anti-IgLON5 disease case reports, making them among the most common features of the disease.

The authors propose that anti-IgLON5 disease should be suspected in younger patients presenting with a dementia with Lewy bodies (DLB)-like picture accompanied by chorea, gaze palsy, early dysphagia, or prominent respiratory symptoms, as these features may serve as red flags distinguishing it from DLB.

Orthostatic hypotension has increasingly been recognized as a common comorbidity of hypertension, with a complex relationship rooted in blood pressure regulation pathophysiology and how OH is derived from two blood pressure measurements.
The statement notes substantial existing evidence that intensive blood pressure treatment does not cause orthostatic hypotension in the majority of patients with essential hypertension.
Some classes of antihypertensive medications may unmask orthostatic hypotension specifically in patients who have underlying autonomic impairment.

The statement recommends short-acting vasoactive agents, including midodrine and droxidopa, alongside countermaneuvers as part of a tailored treatment strategy for OH in hypertensive patients that avoids worsening hypertension.

Midfacial segment pain, described in a few ENP case series, presents as symmetrical pain over the maxillary and ethmoid sinuses without significant sinonasal disease, aura, or autonomic symptoms other than occasional mild nasal congestion or rhinorrhoea.

Nociplastic pain, measured as a surrogate via the ACR Fibromyalgia Survey, was significantly associated with pain-motivated drinking in individuals with alcohol use disorder, independent of confounders and overall pain severity.
Seventy-two percent of participants with alcohol use disorder reported drinking to get relief from physical pain at least some of the time.
Over forty-two percent of participants reported that pain relief motivated their drinking at least half of the time.

The newly developed Pain-Motivated Drinking Scale (PMDS) demonstrated a single-factor structure, strong internal consistency reliability, and construct validity in individuals with alcohol use disorder.
Among 3722 patients presenting with headache, 106 (2.9%) were diagnosed with other primary headache disorders (OPHD).
Of the headache cohort, 52 patients (1.4%) had OPHD alone while 54 (1.5%) had both OPHD and a co-existing primary headache, most often migraine.
All subtypes of other primary headache disorders were reported to be more common in females than males.
The most frequent OPHD subtypes were new daily persistent headache and primary stabbing headache, each accounting for 0.2% of all admitted headache patients.
Photophobia and phonophobia were the most frequently reported symptoms accompanying other primary headache disorders.
Physical activity, stress, and the Valsalva maneuver were the most common triggering factors for other primary headache disorders, at 28.8%, 15.4%, and 15.4% respectively.
Photophobia and phonophobia were the most common symptoms accompanying other primary headache disorders in this cohort.
Physical activity was the most common triggering factor for other primary headache disorders, reported in 28.8% of cases.
Stress was reported as a triggering factor in 15.4% of patients with other primary headache disorders.
The Valsalva maneuver was reported as a triggering factor in 15.4% of patients with other primary headache disorders.

Most triggering factors for headache were more pronounced in patients who had both migraine and another primary headache disorder than in those with OPHD alone, supporting a shared predisposition or 'headache continuum' between migraine and OPHD.
Among 1,046 patients who received an implantable loop recorder for unexplained syncope, 201 (19.2%) had a documented spontaneous asystolic event lasting a median of 10 seconds.
The proportion of patients with spontaneous asystolic reflex syncope documented by implantable loop recorder was statistically identical across the three age tertiles.
In contrast to spontaneous events, the rate of asystolic syncope induced by head-up tilt testing was markedly higher in younger patients and declined with increasing age.

The discordance between age-invariant spontaneous asystole rates and age-dependent tilt-induced asystole rates suggests that head-up tilt testing does not accurately reflect the true age-related behavior of spontaneous reflex syncope.
Migraine is the most prevalent type of primary headache among MS patients, with a reported prevalence of 31%.
The overall prevalence of primary headaches among MS patients is estimated at approximately 56%.
The PRISMS trial reported that 71% of participants treated with interferon-beta-1a experienced headaches.
Cladribine treatment was statistically significantly associated with a higher occurrence of headaches compared to other disease-modifying therapies.
B-cell targeted therapies (ocrelizumab, rituximab, ofatumumab, ublituximab) for MS were not significantly associated with increased headache incidence, contradicting earlier assumptions.
Abnormal trigeminal reflex test results occurred in 89% of patients with MS-related secondary trigeminal neuralgia, compared with only 3% of idiopathic trigeminal neuralgia patients.
Trigeminal neuralgia secondary to MS is bilateral in an estimated 18% of cases, more often than in classical idiopathic trigeminal neuralgia.
In 95% of patients presenting Lhermitte's sign, cervical demyelinating lesions were detected on MRI.
Neuropathic pain is reported by 25% to 90% of MS patients and is a chronic pain condition associated with depression and significant disability.
Chronic pain (nociceptive and neuropathic) occurs in 50-75% of MS patients at some point in their disease course.
Depression is reported in 20% to 40% of MS patients and is an underdiagnosed comorbidity.
White matter hyperintensities are found in more than one-third of female migraine patients, with a higher frequency in migraine with aura.
White matter lesions are present in up to 10% of pediatric migraine patients, occurring earlier in life among migraineurs generally.

Four genetic loci within the major histocompatibility complex have been identified as shared between migraine and multiple sclerosis, suggesting a common genetic susceptibility and that migraine may be a consequence of MS.
Both migraine frequency and MS disease activity were observed to be reduced during pregnancy, implicating hormonal factors in both conditions.
In a small study, initiation of fingolimod therapy led to headache onset within the first week of treatment, persisting for at least three months.
A study of 71 patients suggested that fampridine can cause reactivation of neuropathic pain due to trigeminal neuralgia.
Natalizumab does not appear to aggravate comorbid migraine, although some patients experience headaches as short-term infusion-related reactions.
Migraine occurs more frequently in relapsing-remitting MS patients, while tension-type headache is more frequent in chronic progressive MS patients.
Demyelinating lesions of the brain stem and upper cervical spinal cord (C2 dorsal horn) are associated with headaches in MS patients.
A proposed mechanism links headache exacerbation in MS to dysfunction of the serotoninergic system caused by demyelinating lesions.
Cortical demyelination has been proposed to accelerate cortical spreading depression, a key mechanism in migraine pathophysiology.
Elderly MS patients with longer disease duration and lower SDMT (Symbol Digit Modalities Test) scores more frequently report migraine with aura.
MS patients with comorbid migraine tend to have more severe pain intensity and a higher frequency of headache attacks compared to typical migraine presentation.
The most frequent headache triggers reported in MS patients were fatigue and stress, with weather change and sleepless nights also cited.
Over half of patients treated with disease-modifying therapies exhibited primary headaches, and DMT-treated patients complained more frequently of headache than patients on other therapies.

Presence of dysautonomia at symptom onset, along with coma/lethargy, seizures/status epilepticus, and ICU admission, was significantly associated with worse (higher) CASE and mRS scores at short-term follow-up in anti-NMDAR encephalitis patients.
Weakness present at symptom onset was the only clinical factor that predicted higher (worse) modified Rankin Scale scores at long-term follow-up in anti-NMDAR encephalitis.

ICU admission was associated with worse short-term CASE and mRS scores in anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis patients.

Continuous headache at baseline and the number of previously trialled preventative treatments were the only factors found to be associated with CGRP monoclonal antibody treatment efficacy on subgroup analysis.
Central sensitisation, an amplification of neural signalling in the CNS causing pain hypersensitivity, has been documented as a feature of fibromyalgia.
Features of central sensitisation have also been documented in Ehlers-Danlos syndrome, among other rheumatology-related pain conditions.
There is substantial inter-patient variation in the presence and magnitude of central sensitisation within any given pain condition, underscoring the need for individual assessment.
Central sensitisation is reported to predict poor treatment outcomes across multiple chronic pain patient populations.
Both pharmacological and non-pharmacological strategies have evidence supporting reduction of central sensitisation and improvement of patient outcomes in rheumatology-relevant pain conditions.
The authors propose that matching non-pharmacological and/or pharmacological treatments to central sensitisation-based pain phenotypes could enable precision pain medicine.
Avapritinib produced a significantly greater reduction in total symptom score than placebo over 24 weeks in patients with moderate to severe indolent systemic mastocytosis.

All 20 headache providers interviewed reported asking patients to complete headache diaries.
Most providers (85%) recommended patients track headaches using mobile phones, via in-house apps, free apps, or non-headache-specific software.

Testosterone is proposed as a potential therapeutic target for pain due to its antinociceptive effect.

Human studies support an analgesic effect of testosterone, with higher testosterone levels associated with lower experimental pain sensitivity.

A case report described intravenous oxytocin providing analgesia and migraine relief.

Women who experience migraine have more arginine vasopressin (AVP) receptors on platelets than women without migraine.

An exaggerated blood pressure response to standing (ERTS) is associated with an increased risk of adverse outcomes in both young and old individuals.

The consensus notes that ERTS/OHT has limited reproducibility and recommends confirmation on a second visit assessing supine-to-standing BP changes.
Ambulatory BP monitoring is recommended for most individuals with ERTS/OHT, particularly those with high-normal seated office BP.
Lifestyle changes and close follow-up are recommended for individuals with ERTS/OHT who have normotensive seated office BP.

The consensus recommends ambulatory blood pressure monitoring for most individuals with an exaggerated BP response to standing or orthostatic hypertension, particularly those with high-normal seated office BP.
For individuals with ERTS/OHT and normotensive seated office BP, the consensus recommends implementing lifestyle changes and close clinical follow-up rather than pharmacologic treatment.
It remains unknown whether antihypertensive drug treatment should be administered to individuals with ERTS/OHT who have normotensive seated office BP.
Hypertensive patients who also have ERTS/OHT should be managed using the same standard-of-care approach as any other hypertensive patient.
The consensus calls for standardized standing blood pressure measurement to be implemented in future epidemiological and interventional studies.

Baseline extracellular electrical activity of the trigeminal nerve was higher, with larger amplitude action potentials, in rats with hyperhomocysteinemia compared to controls.
Lower concentrations of KCl were sufficient to increase the frequency of action potentials in trigeminal afferents from hemiskull preparations, indicating a lowered activation threshold.

In trigeminal ganglion neurons from hyperhomocysteinemic rats, the rheobase current needed to elicit an action potential was lower, and more action potentials were fired in response to 2× rheobase stimulation.

In control rats, short-term application of homocysteine and its derivatives increased action potential frequency in the trigeminal nerve and induced calcium transients in neurons, consistent with NMDA receptor activation.
Unlike controls, rats with hyperhomocysteinemia did not show an increased trigeminal nerve response to NMDA application, suggesting altered NMDA receptor sensitivity.
Calcium transient parameters induced by NMDA, homocysteine, and its derivatives were not changed in trigeminal ganglion neurons of rats with hyperhomocysteinemia.

Meningeal mast cells showed increased degranulation in the chronic hyperhomocysteinemia model, whereas acute incubation of meninges with homocysteine or homocysteinic acid did not alter mast cell state.

At a stimulus of twice rheobase, trigeminal ganglion neurons from hyperhomocysteinemic rats generated more action potentials than controls, reflecting enhanced excitability.

In control rats, short-term application of homocysteine and its derivatives increased trigeminal nerve action potential frequency and induced calcium transients in neurons, consistent with activation of NMDA receptors.
In rats with hyperhomocysteinemia, the trigeminal nerve did not show an increased response to NMDA application, unlike controls, suggesting a ceiling or desensitization effect from chronic exposure.

Acute incubation of the meninges in homocysteine and homocysteinic acid did not change the state of meningeal mast cells, indicating that acute exposure is insufficient to trigger degranulation.
In the chronic hyperhomocysteinemia model, meningeal mast cells showed increased degranulation compared to controls, indicating a pro-inflammatory contribution to peripheral migraine sensitization.
Epidemiological data indicate that elevated plasma homocysteine (hyperhomocysteinemia) is associated with increased risk of migraine, particularly migraine with aura.
In prior animal studies, rats with hyperhomocysteinemia exhibited mechanical allodynia, photophobia, and anxiety-like behavior.
Rats with hyperhomocysteinemia showed higher sensitivity to cortical spreading depression than controls in prior work.
Rats with hyperhomocysteinemia were more sensitive in a nitroglycerin-induced model of chronic migraine, suggesting involvement of peripheral nociceptive mechanisms.
The authors propose that controlling homocysteine levels may be a useful strategy for reducing the risk and/or severity of migraine attacks.

Following 12 weeks of supervised heavy resistance training, all 16 participants reported reduced self-nominated knee pain, with a mean decrease of 32.5 mm on a 100 mm VAS.
On a group level, several KOOS subscales improved after the training intervention, though with individual variance.
Fear of movement, measured by the Tampa Scale of Kinesiophobia, decreased on average after the training intervention.
All participants increased quadriceps maximal voluntary contraction (MVC) strength after the 12-week heavy resistance training program, with a mean improvement of 11%.
The largest mean strength improvements, ranging 39–82%, were observed in 5-repetition maximum (5RM) tests across the trained exercises.
Thirteen of 16 participants improved their rate of torque development (RTD) after the training intervention, a factor suggested to protect against symptomatic joint hypermobility.

Knee joint proprioception, measured as mean absolute angle error in a joint position reproduction test, improved in all 16 participants by an average of 55% after training, reaching values similar to non-hypermobile populations.
Patellar tendon stiffness increased in 11 of 16 participants after training, with a mean increase of 11%, comparable to changes seen in healthy adults after similar training.

Heavy resistance training was well tolerated with no major adverse events, good adherence (all completing participants finished at least 88% of sessions), and only minor, manageable pain flares requiring temporary load adjustments in a few cases.

Cranial autonomic symptoms were significantly associated with greater physical impairment on days with mild or no headache in chronic migraine patients.

The patient's anti-NMDAR encephalitis was associated with a newly diagnosed renal cell carcinoma, an atypical tumor trigger compared with the more common ovarian teratoma.

The novel headache was described as an intense painful wave followed by a dull headache, without autonomic symptoms or migrainous features, distinguishing it clinically from typical migraine.
The case highlights that ictal epileptic headache should be considered as a secondary cause of headache in patients with conditions predisposing to epilepsy, such as systemic lupus erythematosus.
Three of 35 patients with suspected multiple system atrophy tested positive for serum and cerebrospinal fluid anti-IgLON5 IgG antibodies using cell-based assays.

The three anti-IgLON5 antibody-positive patients exhibited clinical features overlapping with MSA, including parkinsonism, cerebellar ataxia, severe orthostatic hypotension, acute respiratory failure, sleep parasomnia, vocal cord paralysis, and pyramidal tract signs.

Clinical features atypical for MSA in the anti-IgLON5 antibody-positive patients included myorhythmia, horizontal eye movement restriction, fasciculations, and painful muscle cramps, which may help distinguish anti-IgLON5 disease from MSA.
A genome-wide association study of 888 MSA cases and 7,128 controls identified four genome-wide significant risk loci associated with multiple system atrophy.
Transcriptome-wide association analysis prioritized USP38-DT as a novel susceptibility gene for MSA within one of the identified risk loci.
Transcriptome-wide association analysis prioritized KCTD7 as a novel susceptibility gene for MSA within one of the identified risk loci.
Transcriptome-wide association analysis prioritized lnc-KCTD7-2, a long non-coding RNA, as a novel susceptibility gene for MSA within one of the identified risk loci.
Single-nucleus RNA sequencing analysis showed that MSA-associated risk variants act as cis-expression quantitative trait loci (cis-eQTLs) for multiple genes across both neuronal and glial cell types.
Patients with orthostatic hypotension had significantly higher circulating plasma endostatin levels than controls with a negative tilt test.
Plasma endostatin levels rose progressively across increasing tertiles of orthostatic systolic blood pressure drop.
After adjusting for baseline supine SBP, endostatin levels showed a modest positive linear correlation with the magnitude of orthostatic SBP reduction.

In multivariate logistic regression adjusted for age, sex, BMI, supine BP, antihypertensive medication, cardiovascular disease, risk factors, and cancer, endostatin remained independently associated with OH.
After excluding cancer patients, the independent association between endostatin and OH strengthened slightly in sensitivity analysis.
ROC analysis showed endostatin had moderate discriminative power for predicting orthostatic hypotension, with an optimal cutoff of 47652.8 pg/mL.
Patients with orthostatic hypotension were significantly older than controls.
Prevalence of cancer was significantly higher in OH patients compared with controls.
Prevalence of prior stroke was significantly higher in OH patients compared with controls.
Use of antihypertensive medications was significantly higher in OH patients compared with controls.

Extended regression models showed baseline supine SBP, age, and antihypertensive treatment were each inversely associated with orthostatic SBP drop and endostatin levels, explaining 24-27% of variance.
There was a marginally significant interaction between baseline supine SBP and endostatin levels in predicting orthostatic SBP drop, suggesting endostatin's effect may vary with baseline BP.
Prior work cited in this paper reported that circulating MMP-7 levels are independently associated with orthostatic hypotension and involved in cardiovascular disease promotion.

CVS, once considered a pediatric condition, is now recognized to affect approximately 2% of adults in the United States, a rate similar to pediatric prevalence.

In a pediatric cohort, 40% of 100 children with CVS progressed to chronic autonomic nervous system dysfunction by a mean age of 15 years.

Comorbid conditions identified in CVS patients included anxiety (32%-39%), depression (26%-34%), cardiac conditions (39%-42%), and acid reflux (30%-40%).
A cross-sectional database study from Japan found adult CVS prevalence of 5 per 100,000, much lower than US rates, while pediatric prevalence was much higher at 210 per 100,000.

A whole exome/genome sequencing study identified 12 genes highly likely associated with CVS (affecting cation transport or energy metabolism) and 13 genes possibly related, proposed to induce vagal hyperexcitability and autonomic dysfunction.

The incidence of smoking was higher among cluster headache patients compared to other groups.
